basis: Re-derived independently at baseline 740976ec (no .go file differs between baseline and worktree HEAD: `git diff --stat 740976ec HEAD -- '*.go'` is empty). CENTRAL CLAIM CONFIRMED. Ran `for fn in GetTokens GetTokensByUserID UpdateTokens DeleteTokens DeleteAllUserTokens CleanupExpiredOAuthStates; do git grep -nE "\b$fn\b" 740976ec -- '*.go'; done`. Every one of the six resolves to exactly four files and no others: internal/domain/auth/repository.go (interface decl), internal/adapters/storage/postgres/auth_token_store.go or auth_oauth_state_store.go (impl + its doc comment), internal/testutil/mocks/auth_inmemory.go, internal/testutil/mocks/auth_repository.go. Zero call sites, in production or test, under default or integration tags. This grep is the load-bearing evidence and it is sound for the method-value/method-expression case the lead flagged: a method value (`x.GetTokens`), a method expression (`(*T).GetTokens`), or a func-field wiring must all contain the identifier textually, so the empty result covers them. I also checked the mocks' Fn-field indirection separately -- `git grep -nE '\b(GetTokens|GetTokensByUserID|UpdateTokens|DeleteTokens|DeleteAllUserTokens|CleanupExpiredOAuthStates)Fn\b' 740976ec -- '*.go'` returns only the field declaration and the mock's own nil-check/dispatch inside internal/testutil/mocks/auth_repository.go; no test anywhere assigns any of the six Fn fields. HOLDER COUNT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AND THE FINDING'S COUNT IS WRONG (see what_the_finding_got_wrong): there are THREE holders of an auth.Repository interface value, not two. I enumerated every method called through each -- `git grep -nE '\brepo\.[A-Z][A-Za-z]*' 740976ec -- internal/domain/auth/ internal/adapters/clients/google/` yields StoreOAuthState, ConsumeOAuthState, CreateSession, GetSession, GetUserByID, GetUserByGoogleID, CreateUser, UpdateUser, DeleteSession, DeleteExpiredSessions, UpdateSessionAccess, StoreTokens, IsEmailAllowed, ListAllowedEmails, AddAllowedEmail, RemoveAllowedEmail, ListUsers, SetUserAdmin -- none of the six. cmd/slabledger/main.go's authRepo is assigned at :231 and passed as a constructor arg at :235 and never has a method invoked on it (`git grep -nE '\bauthRepo\b' 740976ec -- cmd/` returns exactly three lines: :222 decl, :231 assign, :235 arg). NEAR-MISS CONFIRMED. internal/adapters/scheduler/session_cleanup.go:77 calls s.authService.CleanupExpiredSessions(ctx), which is auth.Service -> internal/domain/auth/service_impl.go:125 -> repo.DeleteExpiredSessions -> `DELETE FROM user_sessions WHERE expires_at <= $1` (internal/adapters/storage/postgres/auth_session_store.go:184). That is the sessions table, a different table from oauth_states. NOTHING REAPS EXPIRED OAUTH STATES. `git grep -nE '\boauth_states\b' 740976ec` finds exactly three SQL statements: the INSERT in StoreOAuthState, the DELETE in ConsumeOAuthState (which is scoped `WHERE state = $1 AND expires_at > $2`, so it never removes an expired row), and the DELETE in the unwired CleanupExpiredOAuthStates. oauth_states has no FK cascade and no TTL. Every abandoned or expired login attempt therefore leaves a permanent row. Corroborating: migration 000003_supabase_security_and_perf_fixes.up.sql:254 DROPs idx_oauth_states_expires, the index that existed to support exactly this cleanup query -- consistent with the path having been abandoned rather than deliberately removed. My read is that CleanupExpiredOAuthStates is an unwired implementation of behavior the system needs, not dead code: the honest ticket for it is WIRE IT (into session_cleanup.go, which already runs on the right cadence and already holds an auth service), not delete it. CONTRAST -- the five token methods really are removable, and for a reason the finding did not identify: internal/adapters/storage/postgres/migrations/000001_initial_schema.up.sql:104 declares `session_id TEXT REFERENCES user_sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` on user_tokens, so both logout (DeleteSession) and the session-cleanup scheduler (DeleteExpiredSessions) already delete the corresponding token rows at the database level. DeleteTokens and DeleteAllUserTokens are redundant with a live cascade, not a missing cleanup path. TEST SCOPE: no test exercises any of the six. Removing them deletes zero test functions -- only the interface lines, the Postgres impls, the two mock impls, and the six Fn fields. google/oauth_test.go:409 reads repo.Tokens[1], but that map is written by the live StoreTokens (auth_repository.go:113) and survives the removal.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Three defects, none of which overturn the central claim. (1) The holder count is wrong. Evidence #5 asserts "the only other two holders of an auth.Repository-typed variable are cmd/slabledger/main.go's authRepo and google.OAuthService's repo field," and runtime_checks.interface_satisfaction repeats it. There is a third: internal/domain/auth/service_impl.go:24 `repo Repository` (plus the New() parameter at :44), which is unqualified in-package and therefore invisible to the `auth\.Repository` grep the finding used. The finding's own evidence #4 enumerates that holder's call sites separately, so its conclusion survives -- but a verifier trusting the stated count and the stated command would have missed a holder entirely. The count should be three. (2) Evidence #1's output claims each name "resolves to exactly 4 lines"; each actually resolves to 5 lines across 4 files (the doc comment above each implementation matches too). Cosmetic -- the file set is right and the zero-call-site conclusion is right. (3) Substantive: the finding bundles five genuinely-removable methods with one that should not be removed, and its acceptance_criteria do not force the fixer to tell them apart. Criterion 2 reads "git grep for each of the six method names returns no results (or, for whichever is wired instead of removed, shows exactly one new call site...)" -- a fixer can satisfy every criterion by deleting all six, which would make the oauth_states leak permanent and erase the only evidence that the cleanup path was ever intended. The proposed_fix mentions wiring as an option but leaves the choice to the fixer; a mechanical-tier finding must not do that.
